sentences.text: This claim petition is filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .10,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 31.01.2021 at about 11.50 p.m., when petitioner was traveling as an occupant in a Car bearing Regn.No.KA-51-MA-3765 from Tumkur towards Bengaluru, when she reached near Talekere Gate, at that time all of a sudden the said driver of Car drove the same at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and to overtake a lorry lost control over the Car fell into a ditch.

Due to which, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter she was shifted to Prakriya Hospital, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance and nourishment charges etc.
Prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy and was working as a Tailor and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, she became permanent disablement.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Car by its driver.
The respondents being the insurer and owner of offending vehicles are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In pursuance of notice, respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsels and filed their separate written statements.
4. In their written statement, respondent No.1 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
He has also denied age, occupation and income of injured.
He has also denied the place, time and manner of accident.
The petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further contended that as on the date of accident the driver of car had no driving license as on the date of accident.

Further this respondent has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of second respondent in respect of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-51-MA-3765 in Policy No.3001/MI- 09198497/00/000 and valid from 03.09.2020 to 02.09.2021 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
The amount claimed by petitioner his highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.
5. The 2nd respondent in his written statement admitted that he was the owner of Car bearing Regn.No.KA- 51-MA-3765 as on the date of alleged accident.
Further contended that the said motor cycle was insured with ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited vide policy No.300/MI-09198497/00/000 valid from 03.09.2020 to 02.09.2021.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further contended that on the date of accident the petitioner was going as an occupant in a Car, when car reached near Talekere Gate, Bengaluru - Tumkur Road, at that time a Lorry which was going infront of car suddenly applied brake.
As a result of this, the car fell into the ditch.
The amount claimed by petitioner his highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:

sentences.text: ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, she sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 31.01.2021 at about 11.50 p.m, near Talekere Gate, Tumakuru-Bengaluru NH-48 Road, Bengaluru, while she was traveling in a car bearing registration No.KA-51-MA-3765, due to the rash and negligent driving of above said car by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

7. In order to prove case of petitioner, petitioner examined herself as PW.1, Dr.Nagaraj.B.N - Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Centre got examined as PW.2 and MRD Technician at Prakriya Hospital examined as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19 and closed their side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.
8. I have heard the arguments from both sides and perused the material available on record.

9. Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:-
 -:REASONS:-
10. Issue No.1:- In this case the petitioner contend that on 31.01.2021 at about 11.50 p.m., Near Talekere Gate, Tumkur-Bengaluru NH-48 Road, Bengaluru, she had met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-51-MA-3765 driven by its driver and she sustained injuries in the said accident.
11.
The petitioner examined herself as PW.1, in her chief examination she has deposed that due negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle the accident occurred.
In order to prove negligence of driver of offending vehicle, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.1 and 2 FIR and first information.

On perusal of Ex.P.2, one of the occupant in car by name Kum.Divya.V, D/o.Vijaya Kumar the petitioner in MVC.No.865/2021 has lodged first information to police on 01.02.2021, the accident occurred on 31.01.2021.
On the basis of Ex.P.2 police registered a case as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.
She has stated in her first information that due to rash and negligent driving of car the accident occurred.

After registering the case Police went near place of accident and drew up Spot Panchanama and Sketch as per Ex.P.3 & 4 by narrating the place of Smt.B.V.Yamuna vs Icici Lombard Insurance Co. Ltd on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169327361/
3 accident.

sentences.text: The police in Ex.P.4 - Sketch, shown the place of accident.
Ex.P.5 - IMV Report, wherein mentioned the damage caused to vehicle.
The respondent not disprove the Ex.P.1 to 5 documents.
After investigation police filed charge sheet as per Ex.P.6 against driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
The respondents nothing elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner.

Further on perusal of discharge summary, the hospital authorities mentioned that alleged history of RTA, patient was traveling in a car/upside near T.Begur, Tumkur Road at around 12.30 a.m., on 01.02.2021.
The respondent contended that in the hospital in Ex.P.19 - Case sheet it is mentioned that patient was pillion rider traveling on wheeler got colluded to a six wheeler lorry.
As per case sheet, the petitioner was not traveling in car she was traveling in two wheeler, but this car was falsely implicated.
No doubt, on perusal of case sheet in the initial assessment form, it is mentioned as petitioner was a pillion rider traveling on wheeler got colluded to a six wheeler.
It was recorded on 01.02.2021 at 03.00 a.m.
Further on perusal of case sheet, it is mentioned that traveling in a four wheeler got colluded to a six wheeler lorry.

Further, on perusal of case sheet, dated:
01.02.2021 at 9.00a .am., the doctor noted that RTA while traveling in four wheeler sustained injury to left hand.
On perusal of hospital documents, as per initial assessment form, she was a pillion rider, but in other treatment sheets mentioned as she was traveling in four wheeler.
The respondent insurance company did not place any materials before the tribunal to show that the petitioner was pillion rider as on the date of accident and not traveling in car.
Even the respondent insurance company did not elicit any thing from the mouth of PW.1 to establish that she was not traveling in car.
The respondent insurance company has not placed sufficient materials before the tribunal to show that the petitioner was pillion rider and not traveling in car.

So,
in the absence of cogent evidence, this tribunal based upon the MLC Register and police documents considered that petitioner was traveling in four wheeler.
So on perusal of all oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioner, it clearly show that due to negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, the accident occurred.
On meticulous perusal of entire case the respondent did not place any material to disprove the case of petitioner.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.6,
this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-51-MA- 3765 by its driver and petitioner sustained injuries.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of held issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc., let me discussion one by one.
(i) Towards injury and pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident she sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an Smt.B.V.Yamuna vs Icici Lombard Insurance Co. Ltd on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169327361/
4 advice to take follow up treatment.

sentences.text:
In order to prove the injuries caused to her,
petitioner has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7 issued by Prakriya Hospital, wherein diagnosed that petitioner has sustained injury No.1 is grievous and injury No.2 is simple in nature.
So, on perusal of records she took treatment in hospital as an inpatient and the petitioner examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.15 & Ex.P.16.
PW.2/doctor has deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and he assessed the disability for right arm at 46% and to the whole body at 15%.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that she took treatment at Hospital.
The petitioner has produced 5 medical bills for Rs.8,092/- marked at Ex.P.11.
In Ex.P.11 - Bill No.2 & 4 are one and the same, hence this tribunal has considered only one bill.
The petitioner also produced 6 medical bills for Rs.2,668/- marked at Ex.P.12 and one advance receipt marked at Ex.P.10.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
So, Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.9,321/- is just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 31.01.2021 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital.
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner was inpatient at Hospital as she has sustained injuries.
So, during the time of treatment the petitioner also required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner has produced Discharge Summary marked at Ex.P.8, issued by Prakriya Hospital, wherein it shows that petitioner has taken treatment from 01.02.2021 to 04.02.2021 i.e., for a period of 04 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .400/- per day for 04 days to a sum of .1,600/- is just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.
(iv) Towards Conveyance:

The petitioner is the resident of Uppar Palya, Chikka Thotlu Kere Post, Tumkur District, Bengaluru and accident occurred near Talekere Gate, Tumkur-Bengaluru NH-48 Road, Bengaluru, he has admitted for treatment at Hospital.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has produced discharge summary.
Considering the injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of Rs.10,000/- is just and proper towards conveyance charges.
(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:
The petitioner has contended that she was working as a Tailor and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In order to prove his income, the petitioner has not produce any documents to show that she was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

In the absence of positive documents regarding her Smt.B.V.Yamuna vs Icici Lombard Insurance Co. Ltd on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169327361/
5 occupation and income, this tribunal will consider notional income.

sentences.text: Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner might have not attended her regular work at least for a period of 2 months.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2021 at Rs.15,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok Adalat.

So, in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to the Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.
Case on hand the petitioner has not produced any relevant document to prove her income.
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2021 treated as Rs.15,000/- per month as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- (15,000/- x 2) towards loss of income during treatment.
(vi) Towards Permanent Disability:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident, she was inpatient at hospital, and sustained permanent disablement.

The petitioner also examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center, Bengaluru,
examined as PW.2.

entities.text: Sai Ortho and Dental Center, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assessment of disabilities.

The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained pelvis fracture with right sacral ala fracture, right superior and inferior pubic ramus fracture and fracture of the right clavicle and treated conservatively.
The doctor has examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the disability for right arm at 46% and to whole body at 15%.
In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.15 & 16 documents i.e., clinical report and recent X-ray.
The petitioner also examined MRD Technician at Prakriya Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.17 to 19 i.e., authorization letter, MLC Extract and case sheet.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do her work with difficulty.
Therefore, considering all these aspects, the functional disability is assessed at 10%.

In order to prove age of the petitioner, she has produced Ex.P.9 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card, wherein the date of birth is mentioned as 18.09.1988, the accident occurred on 31.01.2021, so the age of petitioner is 33 years as on the date of accident.
Hence, the same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and multiplier '16' is applicable as per Smt. Sarla Verma case.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble supreme court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of her gross income.

entities.text: Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (15,000/- x 12) = Rs.1,80,000/- Loss of future earning p.a. (10% of prior annual income) Rs.18,000/-.

x 16) = Rs.2,88,000/-.
The petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,88,000/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.

(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:-
The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and she is unable to do her day-today activities as earlier.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/-
is just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.

14.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioners are entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
15. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2.

It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-51-MA-3765 by its Smt.B.V.Yamuna vs Icici Lombard Insurance Co. Ltd on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169327361/
7 driver.

sentences.text: The police authorities have not filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.181 of M.V.Act.
So, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .3,98,921/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Ninety Eight Thousand Nine Hundred and Twenty One only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of her Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to her account after expiry of three years period of deposit, without waiting for further order of court.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.6,
this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-51-MA- 3765 by its driver and petitioner sustained injuries.
The petitioner has contended that she was working as a Tailor and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner might have not attended her regular work at least for a period of 2 months.
So, in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to the Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble supreme court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of her gross income.

is just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.
